chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Breast-feeding does not cause prohibition (to marriage) except that which produces flesh and blood.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for breast-feeding to make marriage prohibited in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic consensus that mere sucking does not establish a mahram relationship, requiring instead that the milk be substantial enough to nourish the infant and produce flesh and blood. This criterion distinguishes true nutritional sustenance from temporary intake, a key point of discussion among Shia jurists regarding the minimum quantity (kurr or specific volume) required for permanent prohibition. It underscores the principle that the bond is formed through the physical integration of the milk into the child's body rather than just the act of feeding.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from hammad Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It (marriage) is not Prohibited due to breast-feeding except what builds the flesh and the blood’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Fiammad ibn ‘Uthman who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Breastfeeding does not bring unlawfulness unless it grows flesh and blood.’”
